question: Priya opened a savings account with $182 in it. A holiday bonus from her bank tripled her balance overnight. The next month she paid $166 to cover a family emergency. A matching workplace program then boosted her remaining balance to 8 times its size. She and her brother agreed to split that money in half between their two accounts. Finally, she used $973 of her half to pay off a loan. It had taken her bank 120 minutes, or two hours, to process her very first deposit. How much money, in dollars, did Priya have left after paying off the loan?

Malik started Saturday morning with 163 baseball cards in his collection. By midday, a trading fair had grown his collection to 7 times its original size. In the afternoon, he traded away 889 duplicate cards to other collectors. That evening, his cousin gave him 7 more rare cards as a gift. Later that night, he donated 42 cards to his school's card-collecting club. Malik has been collecting cards for a dozen years now, ever since his grandfather gave him his first pack. How many cards did Malik have in his collection after the donation?

Jordan started the day with 137 marbles in his bag. He lost a match against his friend Sam and had to hand over 96 marbles. Later, Jordan won the next round and got 66 marbles back from Sam. While walking home, he found 31 more marbles that had rolled under the porch. The following day he paid Sam 23 marbles to settle an old bet. That afternoon Jordan won a final game and earned 66 more marbles from Sam. Even with all the back-and-forth, Sam still liked to claim he had more marbles overall. How many marbles did Jordan end up with?

A shipping warehouse counted 81 pallets of ceramic mugs at the start of the day, and each pallet held 8 identical crates, giving the crew the total number of crates awaiting shipment. Every one of those crates in turn held 2 mugs, giving the exact mug count for the shift. During unloading, 630 mugs were found cracked and were pulled from the total. A partner warehouse then sent a matching shipment that grew the remaining mugs to 8 times their count. An inventory clerk found 18 extra mugs overlooked in a corner and added them to the total. Finally, the store's loyalty program awarded 5 points for every mug sold, whereas her colleague Tom's stand across town only ever offered 2 points per mug, and the whole unloading process had taken 90 minutes, which the manager logged as an hour and a half. How many loyalty points did the mugs generate in total?

Elena picked 206 tomatoes from her garden on Saturday. She sold 120 of them at the farmers market that morning. Later she gave 62 more to her neighbor for a fruit swap. She packed what remained evenly into 6 baskets and kept only one basket for herself. Of that basket, 3 tomatoes turned out to be spoiled and had to be thrown away. A local chef then offered to double whatever she had left in exchange for helping at his restaurant. Her friend Marcus, who had grown far fewer tomatoes that season, joked that he'd never catch up to her total. How many tomatoes did Elena end up with?

The Miller orchard started Monday morning with 207 apples in the collection bin. During the morning harvest, 94 apples were pulled out and sent to the cider press. By midday, workers added 19 more freshly picked apples to the bin. In the afternoon, half of the bin's apples were moved to a separate crate for the farmer's market. Later that evening, a neighbor dropped off 6 apples from her own tree. Just before closing for the night, the orchard added 43 more apples gathered from a late round of picking. How many apples were left in the collection bin at the end of the night?

The camera club printed 103 photos for its Saturday exhibit setup in the morning. By afternoon, a bulk-printing discount let them print 7 times as many photos as they'd started with. That evening, a member donated 38 extra photos from an old field trip. Later that night, the club combined every batch with eight other clubs' identical collections, growing the total to 9 times its evening size for the joint city-wide show. Just before midnight, the organizers added 54 last-minute submissions that arrived by email. The exhibit hall itself can seat 300 visitors at a time. How many photos were in the final combined collection?

A downtown parking garage had 56 cars parked when it opened Monday morning. By mid-morning, 16 of those cars had left for work meetings nearby. Throughout the afternoon, 79 more cars pulled in as shoppers arrived at the mall next door. In the early evening, another 15 cars parked for a concert down the street. By closing time that night, 107 cars had driven out to head home. The garage has 4 separate entrances for drivers to use. How many cars were left in the garage when it closed for the night?

Carlos had 152 dollars in his wallet at the start of the day. During the morning, he spent 39 dollars on groceries. By midday, he received 40 dollars back as a refund for a returned item. In the afternoon, he paid 121 dollars toward a phone bill. That evening, a friend repaid him 13 dollars he was owed. Just before bed, he spent another 36 dollars on a late dinner, even though the restaurant was only a 5-minute walk from his apartment. How much money did Carlos have left in his wallet by the end of the night?

Nina had 106 points in the school reading challenge. After finishing three more books that week, she earned 33 additional points. A bonus weekend then doubled her entire point total. She lost 168 points when a mix-up in the record system wiped out some of her entries. After the error was partly corrected, she still had to forfeit 82 more points for a late submission. Her classmate Tara, who had a much smaller total all along, ended up passing her in the rankings anyway. How many points did Nina have after the penalty?

The school charity jar held 202 dollars at the start of the fundraiser. On the first day, the jar's coins were miscounted and 23 dollars had to be removed from the total after a recount. The next day, students donated 64 more dollars during the morning assembly. On day three, a bake sale added 36 dollars to the jar. A local business then matched part of the donations with 63 more dollars. Finally, a surprise raffle contributed another 58 dollars, though the raffle tickets themselves had been printed in a run of 500. Two organizers, Priya and Sam, noticed that Priya's personal collection can had far more coins in it than Sam's. How much money was in the charity jar after the raffle donation?

A grocery store's rice storage held 56 kilograms at the start of Monday morning. By mid-morning, half of that rice had been sold off to a wholesale buyer, leaving only the remaining half in storage. In the afternoon, a delivery truck dropped off 14 more kilograms. Later that afternoon, another supplier brought in 75 additional kilograms. That evening, a supply agreement brought the store's rice total to 7 times what it had been. Just before locking up for the night, the store shipped out 782 kilograms to a partner branch across town, even though that branch is only 3 kilometers away. How many kilograms of rice were left in storage after the shipment?

A stationery shop had 196 notebooks on its shelves at the start of the month. A supplier delivered 17 more notebooks the following week. A school bulk-order then took 175 notebooks off the shelves. A few days later, 25 notebooks were returned as damaged and removed from stock. Near the end of the month, a new shipment added 67 notebooks to the shelves. A holiday sale then brought in enough customers that the shop's remaining stock needed to be replenished to 4 times its size to meet demand, a demand the owner hadn't seen in a dozen years of running the shop. How many notebooks were on the shelves after the restock?

A small food truck business had 148 dollars in its account after a slow start to the season. A viral social media post then brought in enough new customers that the account balance grew to 9 times its earlier amount. The owner paid 293 dollars to restock ingredients for the following week. A catering client then paid an extra 19 dollars as a tip. Regular weekend sales added 63 dollars more to the account. A costly refrigerator repair cost the business 896 dollars. Finally, a franchise partner made an investment that brought the account balance to 4 times its size. How much money was in the food truck's account after the investment?

A beekeeper began spring with 201 jars of honey in storage. A record wildflower bloom left her with 5 times as many jars by the end of the season. A regional co-op then combined her stock with matching batches from other hives, leaving her with 9 times as many jars as she had after the bloom. A neighbor donated 12 extra jars bottled at home. A wholesale buyer purchased 6564 jars for a chain of cafes. She then filled 71 more jars from a late-season batch. A nearby stand priced eggs at 4 dollars a dozen, which had nothing to do with her honey count. How many jars of honey did the beekeeper have in the end?

Marcus had 85 dollars in his wallet at sunrise. In the morning, he earned 25 more dollars helping a neighbor move furniture. In the afternoon, he spent 61 dollars on new running shoes and another 38 dollars on a bicycle tune-up. That evening, his cousin gave him an amount equal to what remained, making his money 2 times as much as before. A shop window that evening advertised sneakers for 99 dollars, though he didn't buy any. How much money did Marcus have by the end of the evening?

Priya kept a single running tally of pages read this month, starting at 205 pages. She read 74 more pages on a bus ride, then 66 more later that day. Her book club then had 9 branch locations each log the identical total in her honor, making her recorded count 9 times as large. The branch meeting itself ran for 90 minutes, which organizers rounded to an hour and a half on the schedule. Afterward, she donated credit for 1073 pages to a member who had fallen behind. How many pages did Priya's tally show in the end?

Diego was cataloguing rare trading cards for his shop, starting with 134 cards in a single binder. A booster restock left him with 5 times as many cards as before. He then sold 234 cards to a passing collector. A friend gave him 8 more cards found in an old drawer. That evening, a rival dealer named Wallace, who had exactly half as many cards as Diego started with, watched enviously as a warehouse delivery gave Diego 6 times as many cards as he then had. A nearby table displayed a sticker album for 17 dollars, which nobody bought. How many cards did Diego end up with?

A candle maker began the week with 78 finished candles in stock. She made 29 more candles for a wedding order. A bulk retailer then took candles amounting to 8 times her stock for a regional order, and a national chain multiplied that new count by 7 for its own warehouses. A rival shop across town sold similar candles for 15 dollars apiece, unrelated to this shipment. The chain later returned 1818 candles that hadn't sold during a slow month. A dozen scented sachets sat untouched on a nearby shelf, playing no part in the candle count. How many candles did the candle maker have left?

A stamp collector had 36 stamps in his album at sunrise. In the morning, he bought 54 more stamps at a flea market. By midday, a rare trade with a dealer left him with 9 times as many stamps as before. In the afternoon, his sister gave him 13 more stamps, and a cousin later added 54 more from an old family collection. That evening, he found 48 more stamps tucked inside a forgotten book. How many stamps did he have by the end of the evening?

A used bookstore had 126 novels on its clearance shelf, and the owner added 31 more from a donated box. A book club then bought in bulk for branch libraries, leaving the shelf with 8 times as many novels. 41 books were later returned as damaged and pulled from stock. A regular customer mentioned the store was about a dozen steps from the coffee shop, unrelated to the books. The delivery van spent 90 minutes on the road, roughly an hour and a half, on a special drop-off. 71 more books then arrived from an estate sale, and 65 more came in from a closing school library. How many novels did the store end up with?

A trail runner logged 121 miles on her training app at the start of the season. A GPS correction removed 7 miles from her total. Her coach then had her repeat that distance across a relay, leaving her with 4 times as many logged miles. A regional series required 8 teams to each log the same relay total, multiplying her recorded miles by 8. The series then combined totals across 8 identical divisions nationwide, multiplying the number once more. Her training that week also took about 300 minutes, which is exactly 5 hours. How many miles did the leaderboard record for her by the end?

A toy factory packed 120 action figures onto a single pallet. A bundling machine left the pallet with 4 times as many units after adding accessory packs. A second station repeated the same process, again leaving the pallet with 4 times as many units as before. A retailer then canceled part of the order, pulling 1711 units from the shipment. A separate quality-control line nearby processed about a dozen unrelated toy cars that day. The remaining stock was then replicated across 6 regional warehouses, leaving 6 times as many units. How many action figure units ended up going to the warehouses?

Two clubs, the Eagles and the Hawks, both track ticket sales, but this story follows only the Eagles' running total, which started at 230 tickets, already ahead of the Hawks' count. A promotional weekend tripled the Eagles' ticket total. A weekday sale then added 19 more tickets, and a group booking added 49 more. A student discount event brought in 24 more tickets, and a final walk-up rush added 49 more. The Hawks, meanwhile, were rumored to have sold around 400 tickets, a separate tally from the Eagles'. How many tickets had the Eagles sold in total?

A farmer had 57 crates of peaches at sunrise. In the morning, 24 crates were sold at a roadside stand. By midday, a wholesale buyer took enough that the remaining crates became 5 times as many. In the afternoon, a second orchard sent over 50 more crates, and a co-op added 67 more. That evening, a final delivery brought 59 more crates, after a drive that took about 120 minutes, right around 2 hours. How many crates of peaches did the farmer have by the end of the evening?
